main_text.l: st. preciosior in conscientia sua erat sacra Dei
lex & sanctio, quàm ut pauperie vel gentili-
ùm fauore induceretur ad illicita obeunda;
sicut & Daniel cum socijs in Babylone,
Joseph in Ægypto, Judith in castris Holofer-
nis, Gen.43.Judith 12. Omnia quidem mun-
da sunt mundis. Verùm legis Mosaicæ ri-
tus usque ad Christum Judæis omnibus ob-
servandus erat, & idolatriæ occasio summa
diligentia evitanda. Polluebantur igitur
Israelitæ ferè omnes, i.e. plurimi contra legem
agendo, quam Tobias summopere semper
observare satagebat, ne peccaret in Deum,
& contra conscientiam illicita sumeret, cum
licita per Dei gratiam non deessent. Atque
huius sanctitatis præmium Tobias etiam in
hoc mundo accepit. Donatus est enim a re-
ge Salmanasar libertate, ut illi licuerit per-
gere & operari, ut voluit. Sed ipse hac sua
libertate, ex gratia Dei (cuius opera & fe-
rræ, & tyranni mansuefieri, velint nolint,
coguntur) accepta, non abusus est: sed iti-
tans ad omnes captiuos, eos salutariter mo-
nuit atque confolatus est. Porrò quæ salutis
monita fuerint, quæ illis dedit Tobias, vide-
ris in commentarijs Pellicani. Exhortatus
enim est concaptiuos ad tolerantiam exilij, ad
obedientiam regi præstândam, etiamsi immo
destior & discolus iam eis contigisset, quado
id Domino placuisse viderent ex facto, pœ-
nam esse codignam criminibus non possent
ignorare: forti animo omne solum patriam

page.notes: The running head "NVPTIALES." and the page number "191" are read from a small-capital, partly worn print; check them. The opening fragment "st." (from "est") is cut off at the line start and stays a fragment. Doubtful readings: "Gen.43." (the number after "Gen." is faint); "ferræ" in "ferè" line, and "si" in "etiamsi" and "destior" (printed "destior", kept as printed); "quado" is printed as such and kept. Words corrected only by the u/v and i/j rules: vsque, Judæis, Iudith, Ioseph, Christum, evitanda, concaptiuos. The punctuation "obeunda;" and "abusus est:" is taken from the scan as printed. The line "tans ad omnes captiuos" begins with "iti-" at the line end, kept with its printed hyphen. A small star mark near the foot is a printer's or scan mark, not text, and is left out.
